concept.name: European-style option
concept.definition: An option that may be exercised only on its expiration date; most (but not all) U.S. index options use European-style exercise.
concept.intuition: A European option is a single-day right: you can trade the contract any time, but you can invoke the strike only on expiration day itself.
concept.mechanics: The holder can always close the position by selling the option in the market before expiration; only exercise is restricted to the expiry date (and the last trading day is typically the day before expiration for index options). With no early-exercise possibility, European options are simpler to price (e.g., Black-Scholes applies directly) and writers face no early-assignment risk.
concept.failure_modes: Holders needing to monetize before expiry must sell into the market, so wide bid-ask spreads or halted trading can trap value; confusing a European index option's last trading day with its expiration date can leave a position held unintentionally through settlement.
concept.misconceptions: European-style does not mean the position is locked until expiry — closing trades are always possible; nor does the name imply the option trades in Europe.
concept.example: A European-style index call can only be exercised at expiration, and its last trading day is usually the Thursday before expiration Friday; a holder wanting out on Tuesday simply sells the option on the exchange.
